title: UGC wireless headphones unboxing ad, 7 shots
prompt_text:
I made this entire product ad with Veo in minutes.
Prompt:
Create a high-energy, realistic User Generated Content (UGC) product advertisement featuring a man in his mid-to-late 20s unboxing and testing a pair of premium wireless noise-cancelling headphones. The video should feel like authentic smartphone footage captured at home, not a traditional commercial. Use rapid jump cuts, satisfying ASMR sounds, natural reactions, realistic movements, and cinematic product close-ups.
PRODUCT: SONARA X1 WIRELESS HEADPHONES. Premium over-ear headphones featuring a matte-black finish, brushed aluminum hinges, soft memory-foam ear cushions, a slim padded headband, a touch-control panel on the right ear cup, a subtle glowing LED status light, and a sleek hard-shell carrying case.
SHOT 1: THE ARRIVAL [Medium shot, eye-level] The man sits on his living room couch with a delivery box branded "SONARA X1" on his lap. He grabs the sealing tape and tears it open in one satisfying motion. SFX: Loud, crisp tape ripping sound.
SHOT 2: THE REVEAL [Medium shot, slightly low angle] He opens the box, lifts out the hard-shell carrying case, and unzips it to reveal the headphones nested inside. He looks genuinely impressed. Dialogue: "Okay, these finally came!" SFX: Cardboard movement, zipper opening, case lid clicking.
SHOT 3: THE PRODUCT CLOSE LOOK [Full shot, clean jump cut] He holds the SONARA X1 headphones up in front of the camera, peels off the protective film from the ear cups, and runs his thumb along the brushed aluminum hinge. He flexes the headband and presses the soft ear cushions. Dialogue: "Look at this! The build quality is crazy." SFX: Protective film peeling, subtle metallic clicks, soft foam compressing.
SHOT 4: FIRST CONNECTION [Close-up sequence] Show him holding the power button until the LED light glows blue. His phone screen lights up showing a pairing pop-up, and he taps "Connect." He slides the headphones over his ears. Dialogue: "Alright, let's see what these can do." SFX: Power-on chime, Bluetooth connection tone, soft cushion seal.
SHOT 5: THE NOISE-CANCELLING TEST [Close-up, 45-degree angle] A TV plays loudly in the background and a fan whirs nearby. He double-taps the touch panel to activate noise cancellation. His eyes widen as the room noise drops away, and he slowly nods to the beat. SFX: Background noise abruptly muffled, activation chime, soft bass thump.
SHOT 6: THE FINAL EXPERIENCE [Medium shot, eye-level] He leans back on the couch, closes his eyes for a few seconds, lightly drums his fingers on his knee, then lifts one ear cup and smiles directly at the camera. Dialogue: "Wait... I think I'm never taking these off!"
SHOT 7: HERO PRODUCT SHOT [Slow cinematic close-up] The SONARA X1 headphones rest on a wooden side table beside the open carrying case and a phone showing a music playlist. Soft natural window light reflects across the matte-black finish and aluminum hinges. Final dialogue: "This is officially my new favourite upgrade."
VIDEO STYLE: - Vertical 9:16 format. - Ultra-realistic smartphone footage. - Natural human movements and expressions. - Fast-paced jump cuts. - Crisp product details. - Realistic button presses, LED glow, and ear cushion compression. - Authentic ASMR sound design. - Natural indoor lighting. - No artificial-looking CGI. - Consistent product design across every shot. - Accurate hand movements and realistic product interactions. The final result should look like a genuine viral product-review video filmed by a real customer.

title: Vertical Remotion short with constrained motion and Whisper timing
prompt_text: Aqui vai. Cola no Claude junto com as imagens e o áudio: "Monte um short vertical 1080x1920 em Remotion. Cada imagem fica na tela exatamente o tempo da frase dela (use os timestamps de palavra do Whisper). Movimentos permitidos, só estes: zoom lento de 3 a 5% por cena, parallax entre fundo e personagem em camadas separadas, e entrada com ease-out de 12 frames. Proibido girar, quicar ou tremer. Corte seco entre cenas. Antes do render final, exporte um frame parado do meio de cada cena pra eu revisar." Se ainda ficar tosco, manda um print de um desses frames que eu vejo o que tá pegando.
